items.title: 60499_Garvin Bushell oral history interview
items.q: Jabob Smith, Gus Akins, and those guys came out of Fred Cooley... That band traveled all over the world... And except Willy Gant the rest of us were geechees out of South Carolina and from Jenkins Orphanage

ctx.x: 135th Street and Fifth Avenue, down in the cellar. I remember one night they beat up on a fellow and they put him out. He shot the doorman upstairs, he came down the stairs and stood at the foot of the stairs and just starts shooting across the cabaret. Well, our piano set back in a little alcove like, and we had six in the band -- we had a tuba, then --

incidentally, these were Jenkins boys that worked in this cabaret, all from Jenkins Orphanage. In those days the best brass men in the country, Jabbo Smith, Gus Akins, and those guys came out of Fred Cooley, clarinet player, [unintelligible] came out of [Kewley] L.A. Jenkins Orphanage from South Carolina. That band traveled all over the world and played on street corners for collection, that's how they kept the school going -- it was an orphanage school. And except Willy Gant the rest of us were geechees out of…
Well, how did you manage -- the group manage to consistently work -- is this something you get used to or --
